title: Trait selection meeting a prescribed generic open with finite fraction field
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $K$, generic point $\eta$ and closed point $s$ of $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $Y$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] of finite type over $S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], whose structural map is dominant, meaning that its image is dense in $S$. Suppose that the fibre $Y_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is nonempty. For every nonempty open subscheme $U\subseteq Y_\eta$ [def-weil-open-immersion] there exist a discrete valuation ring $R_0$, a local injective homomorphism $R\to R_0$, a finite extension $K_0/K$ of fraction fields [def-pc-field-extension] (finite-dimensional as a $K$-vector space), and an $S$-morphism $c:\operatorname{Spec}R_0\to Y$ whose generic restriction factors through $U$ and whose closed point maps into $Y_s$. Neither excellence nor completeness of $R$ is assumed; $R_0$ is not required to be finite as an $R$-module.

source.place: Tag 05GU, more-morphisms-lemma-quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open-X, applied at a closed point of the special fibre, followed by Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr, applied to the local integral curve selected there. The latter is in literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $t$ of $R$. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], every ideal of $R$ is principal, hence finitely generated, so $R$ is Noetherian and $S$ is locally Noetherian. Every nonzero prime $\mathfrak p=(a)$, with $a\ne0$, equals $(t)$: write $a=tb$ since $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m_R$; primality gives $t\in\mathfrak p$ or $b\in\mathfrak p$, and the latter gives $b=ac=tbc$, hence $1=tc$, impossible. Thus $D(t)=\{(0)\}$. The domain $R[1/t]$ is a field, since a nonzero nonunit would lie in a nonzero maximal ideal by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal], whose contraction would be a nonzero prime of $R$ avoiding $t$: a nonzero fraction in that maximal ideal has nonzero numerator in its contraction. Consequently $R[1/t]=K$ and $\eta=D(t)$ as open subschemes. Thus the given $U$ is open in $Y$. Choose an affine open $X=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$ meeting $Y_s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], $B$ is a finite type $R$-algebra. The ideal $tB$ is proper because $X_s$ is nonempty. Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq tB$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal]. Its point $x$ is closed in $X_s=\operatorname{Spec}(B/tB)$, by the affine spectrum description [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-scheme-fibre].

source.place: Tag 05GU, hypotheses; choice of a closed point after restriction to an affine open meeting the special fibre. Algebra Tag 00E0, algebra-lemma-Zariski-topology, maximal ideal existence.

proof.text: The integral scheme $Y$ is irreducible [def-pc-integral-scheme], and has a generic point $\xi$ by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. The defining equality $\overline{\{\xi\}}=Y$ means that $\xi$ belongs to every nonempty open, hence to $U$ and $X$, and specializes to $x$. Since $U\subseteq Y_\eta$, its image is $\eta\ne s$. Apply [lem-sfb-quasi-section-nearby-open] to $X\to S$, the point $x$, and the open $U\cap X$. It gives an integral closed subscheme $Z\subseteq X$ with generic point $z\in U\cap X$, containing $x$, and quasi-finite over $S$ at $x$. All hypotheses are now verified: the morphism is locally of finite type, $S$ is locally Noetherian, $x$ is closed in its fibre, and $\xi$ is the required nearby point.

source.place: Tag 05GU, more-morphisms-lemma-quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open-X, application and the reduced-closure construction in its proof.

proof.text: By the affine description of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], $Z=\operatorname{Spec}C$ for a quotient $C$ of $B$. Images of the finite $R$-algebra generators of $B$ generate $C$, so $Z\to S$ is of finite type. Hence $Z$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. By [lem-sc-quasi-finite-points-open], the quasi-finite locus $Q\subseteq Z$ is open, contains $x$, and is locally quasi-finite over $S$. Choose an affine open neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}E$ of $x$ inside $Q$. The open $W$ contains $z$: otherwise the closed complement $Z\setminus W$ would contain $z$, hence its closure $Z$, contradicting $x\in W$. The integral affine $W$ is quasi-compact, and $W\to S$ is locally quasi-finite by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-restriction-to-opens] applied to $Q\to S$, the open $W\subseteq Q$ and $V=S$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-qc-source-bounded-fibres] gives that $W_\eta$ is the spectrum of a finite-dimensional $K$-algebra $D$. By [lem-sbc-affine-fibre-sections-tensor] applied to $W\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, the affine open $W$ itself and the prime $(0)$, $D=\Gamma(W_\eta,\mathcal O)\cong E\otimes_R\kappa(\eta)=E\otimes_R K$, compatibly with $E\to D$; since $K=R[1/t]$ by step 1, $D=E[1/t]$.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01TI (lemma-quasi-finite-points-open), 03JA (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-qc-source-universally-bounded). Tag 01TH (4) for restriction to the open W; affine fibre ring as a tensor product.

proof.text: Put $L=\kappa(z)=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] applied to $Z$ and $W$, $E$ is an integral domain and $L$ is its fraction field. The point $z$ lies over $\eta$, giving the inclusion $K\hookrightarrow L$; consequently the structural map $R\to E\hookrightarrow L$ is injective. In particular $t$ remains nonzero. The map $E[1/t]\to L$ sends $e/t^n$ to its fraction in $L$; it is injective because $E\hookrightarrow L$ is injective and $t\ne0$. It extends the structural inclusion $K=R[1/t]\hookrightarrow L$, so it identifies the generic-fibre algebra $D$ with a $K$-subalgebra of $L$. Thus $D$ is a nonzero domain with fraction field $L$. Since $D$ is finite-dimensional over $K$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field] makes it a field. It equals $L$: every element of $L$ is $a/b$ for $a,b\in E$, $b\ne0$, and $b$ already has an inverse in the field $D$. Hence $L/K$ is finite. Set $K_0=L$.

source.place: Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions; Tag 03JA, finite generic fibre; elementary fraction-field identification of a localization that is a field.

proof.text: The points $x,z\in Z$ are distinct, since their images in $S$ are $s$ and $\eta$. Apply [lem-sfb-nongeneric-point-same-field-dvr] to the integral locally Noetherian $Z$, its generic point $z$, and its nongeneric point $x$. We obtain a discrete valuation subring $R_0\subseteq L$ with fraction field exactly $L$ and a morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}R_0\to Z$ whose closed point maps to $x$ and whose generic restriction is the canonical $\operatorname{Spec}L\to Z$. Composing with $Z\hookrightarrow X\hookrightarrow Y$ gives $c$. Its generic point maps to $z\in U$; the canonical generic-point morphism therefore factors through the open $U$. Its closed point maps to $x\in Y_s$.

source.place: Tag 054F, properties-lemma-locally-Noetherian-specialization-dvr, same-field case; algebraic input Tag 00PH, algebra-lemma-exists-dvr.

proof.text: Equip $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ with the $S$-structure given by the composite $c$ followed by $Y\to S$; then $c$ is an $S$-morphism by construction. Let $R\to R_0$ be its affine ring map. Its composite into $K_0=L$ is $R\hookrightarrow K\hookrightarrow L$, since the generic restriction is the canonical generic-point morphism. It is therefore injective and induces the finite extension $K_0/K$ from step 4. On affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the image of the prime $\mathfrak m_{R_0}$ is its inverse image in $R$. Since that image is the closed point $s$, the inverse image is $\mathfrak m_R$. Hence the ring map is local; injectivity lets us write this as $\mathfrak m_{R_0}\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$. These are all the requested conclusions. The construction never asserted that $R_0$ is module-finite over $R$.

source.place: Tag 00PH, domination conclusion; affine spectrum functor applied to the constructed composite.
